sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area between the Basilicata and Puglia regions, from the city of Potenza (west) to north of the city of Taranto (east), and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. S-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a number of intermediate seismicity in this region. However, the western sector of the area was hit by some relevant earthquake, including the 13 February 1963 (Mw 5.3, Tito), and 6 August 1954 (Mw 5.3, Pietragalla) ones. Above all, the area is known for the 5 May 1990-26 May 1991 (Mw 5.8 and 5.2, respectively) Potentino sequence.
This Source is thought to be a deep, blind E-W fault system, a part of the tectonic mechanism that seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. The western sector of this source includes the causative fault of the 1990 earthquake, an event whose seismological parameters closely resemble the characteristics of the well studied 2002 Molise sequence that has occurred way north of this area. The 1990-91 sequence has shown that the mechanism that governs the present-day right-lateral reactivation of deep, long-lived, regional shear zones that affect the Adriatic foreland is not confined to the segments illuminated by the 2002 Molise earthquakes, but rather suggests the existence of a broad seismogenic domain â€“ which poses new issues concerning its possible explanation and interaction (if any, and at what depth ranges) with extension along the Apennines.
To the west, this source gives way to the NW-SE trending, main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
A segment of this Source has been associated with the key earthquake that has affected this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped subsurface structures. The dip was based on seismological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents right-lateral strike slip, based on seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on seismological and subsurface data. The slip rate was inferred from geodynamic considerations for the tectonic environment that includes this source.
